note: Assumptions for the I/O and power estimate shown on the console while Left Alt is held (panels/virtual/budget.js). Rough figures, to compare modules and see which board a grouping overloads; change them as the parts are chosen.

olimex-esp32-poe2.name: Olimex ESP32-POE2
olimex-esp32-poe2.note: from PoE (802.3at), 25 W in all: 5 V 1.5 A (7.5 W) for the display drivers and 5 V LEDs; 12 V 1.5 A (18 W, the jumper on 12 V, not 24 V) for 12 V lamps; 3.3 V 1 A for the ESP32 and Ethernet (logic_w, about 0.75 W)

olimex-esp32-poe.name: Olimex ESP32-POE
olimex-esp32-poe.note: 4 W (0.8 A at 5 V, the 3.3 V rail taken from it) from PoE, per Olimex; the ESP32 with Ethernet takes about 0.75 W

raspberry-pi.name: Raspberry Pi
raspberry-pi.note: a glass module: the Pi and its screen have their own supply; only the panel's I/O is counted

mcp23017.note: I2C expander: switches, buttons, rotary positions, keypad lines, lamps

max7219.note: 8 rows of 8 LEDs: a 7-segment digit per row, or 8 bar segments or matrix dots; 20 mA segments (RSET), 160 mA with every segment lit, about 32 mA with 40 % lit at half intensity

uln2803.note: a driver for lamps on a rail above 5 V: the expanders switch it, it switches 8 lamps

lamps.note: led: a 5 mm indicator LED (above a switch, or alone); lamp: a lit push button, 12 V with its resistor built in (as many are sold); cell: an annunciator cell, a light box with plain LEDs behind its legend (leds per cell, ma per LED). typical_on: the share lit in flight. Change a v to move that load to another rail: above 5 V it goes through ULN2803 drivers

rgb.note: an addressable RGB LED (WS2812B / SK6812): about 20 mA for one colour at full, 60 mA white (all three); one data pin drives the chain

pins.note: ESP32 pins: the shared I2C bus, the MAX7219 chain, a buzzer on its own PWM pin
